notes: Asserts the scenario's full arc: ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready, with the SECOND waiting episode raised by a READ-ONLY tool (Read) and the first by a mutating one (Write), in one session and one turn. Both gates are forced deterministically by a project-local PreToolUse hook returning permissionDecision=ask for Write|Read, so neither depends on Claude Code's allowlist heuristics; the same hook appends to .gate-hook.log so the recording carries positive proof that both gates actually opened (see the cell's vacuous-pass caveat — one waiting episode is what a missing second gate and the bug under test produce alike). KNOWN FAILING on main (#1861): readonly_gate_waiting is the phase that fails. The daemon installs PermissionRequest with a nine-alternative tool-name matcher (hookinstaller.go, hookMatcher) that excludes Read, so PermissionPending is never set and ClassifyState rule 0 never fires; no lower rung re-derives it either (isUserBlockingTool and isPermissionGatedEditTool both exclude Read), so the ladder falls through to transcript_activity -> working and the session reads working for the whole time the modal is on screen. PR #1867 (open, unmerged) widens the matcher to "*"; this spec deliberately asserts the CORRECT behaviour and is NOT weakened to match the bug. No count is pinned beyond the two the scenario itself asserts as its subject: the two episodes are the claim, not an incidental cycle count. model is left unpinned for record to fill from the recording.

text: Session appears in ready after launch
The Write tool call is gated: modal opens, session -> waiting. This is the half 2-19 already covers; it is here so one recording can tell the two tool classes apart.
User answers the Write dialog; the write executes and the turn resumes -> working

THE ASSERTION UNDER TEST. The Read tool call is gated and must produce its OWN waiting episode, not be skipped and not be merged into the Write episode. Fails on main: PermissionRequest is installed with a nine-tool matcher that excludes Read, and no lower classifier rung re-derives the prompt (#1861).
User answers the Read dialog; the read executes and the turn resumes -> working
Turn ends -> ready. The session does not remain waiting after the last dialog closes.
Trailing idle: the session stays ready for >=10 s after the last dialog, catching a session left pinned at, or falling back to, waiting.
